name: Robotaxis and autonomous driving
summary: Vehicles handle the driving task within an approved operating area, with passenger services providing the clearest commercial proof.
useCase: A rider orders an unattended taxi inside a mapped city service area; the same vehicle may still be unavailable in a nearby suburb or severe weather.
whyNow: Waymo has moved from tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of weekly driverless trips. This establishes repeat demand in selected cities, while safety, fleet servicing and geographic permission still constrain expansion.

mainstream.scope: Routine paid driverless taxi service in a substantial set of dense, approved urban markets; not universal autonomous driving.
mainstream.rationale: The operating base supports city-by-city expansion before 2030. Wider weather coverage, lower fleet cost and regulatory acceptance determine whether that becomes ordinary urban transport. A safety incident or poor economics can delay individual markets beyond 2035.

metric.name: Waymo weekly fully autonomous trips
metric.scope: One operator, served markets; company-reported lower-bound snapshots
metric.limitations: These are lower-bound weekly snapshots, not annual totals or global robotaxi adoption. Service territory expands between observations. The 2026 point is current to the source, not a full-year average.
metric.futureNote: Waymo has an end-2026 weekly-trip target, shown separately as a company goal. It is not treated as an observed annual data point or an industry-wide growth forecast.

milestones.text: Commercial robotaxi operation existed, but no comparable 2021 weekly observation is included.
No comparable 2022 weekly observation was established in this review; pilots and limited operating domains remain the historical context.
Waymo reported more than 10,000 weekly public driverless rides across San Francisco and Phoenix.
Waymo reported 150,000-plus weekly trips in its December year review.
Waymo reported more than 14 million trips during 2025 by its December review and set a goal of one million weekly trips by end-2026.
The current company sustainability page reports 500,000-plus weekly fully autonomous EV trips. Toronto was announced for 2028, not operating in Canada at cutoff.

tailwinds: Repeat passenger demand in deployed markets
Improved vehicle utilisation as service zones connect
Fleet, mapping and chip suppliers sell infrastructure as operators expand
bottlenecks: Safety must hold across rare events and poor weather
Cleaning, charging, insurance and remote assistance reduce the apparent labour saving
watchMetrics: Paid rides per vehicle per day and contribution margin, not just announced cities
Rider-only miles and injury outcomes using comparable exposure
Share of the metropolitan population actually inside an unrestricted service area
